3. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that opposite party 2 as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Suit No.13 of 2018 in the aforesaid Adalat against the petitioner for recovery of loan. The petitioner was defendant 1 in the suit. The petitioner appeared in the suit and filed written statement. After holding trial, the Adalat decreed the suit on 5-4-2017. Opposite party 2 then filed the aforesaid execution case before the same Court. In the execution case, they calculated the decreetal amount at Taka 5.58,70,503 with interest. The bank then prayed for publishing auction notice to sell the mortgaged land and accordingly the Adalat passed order of auction sale which was published on 21-1-2019 in the daily newspaper. In the meantime, the petitioner filed an application before the Adalat under Order 21 rule 83 of the Code read with section 57 of the Ain, 2003 stating grounds that he is willing to sell the mortgaged property detailed in the schedule of the decree through private negotiation. He further stated in the application that the market price of the property would be more than the amount claimed by the bank. He undertook there that he will adjust the entire outstanding amount. Therefore, he prayed for issuing a certificate to sell the land as prescribed by the Adalat. The decree holder bank did not raise any objection against the said application but the Adalat without applying the judicial mind by the order under challenge rejected the said application and directed the bank to take necessary steps and to issue notice fixing date of auction. 

 5. Mr M. Mohiuddin Yousuf, learned Advocate for opposite party No.2 submits that the Adalat on correct appreciation of fact and law rejected the application of the petitioner filed under Order 21 rule 83 read with section 57 of the Ain, 2003. He refers to the cases of Somali Bank Limited, Head Office vs Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, No.1, Chattogram and others, 5 ALR 381 and the case of Agrani Bank vs Anwarul Bashir Khan and others, /9 BLC (AD) 120 and submits that under the provisions of section 33 of the Ain and the provisions of sub-rule 3 of rule 83 of Order XXI the application filed by the judgment-debtor cannot not be entertained. Sub-rule 3 of the aforesaid rule and order is a non-obstante clause which provides "Nothing in this rule shall be deemed to apply to a sale of property directed to be sold in execution of decree for sale in enforcement of a mortgage of, or charge on, such property". Admittedly the petitioner mortgaged the land to the bank and defaulted in payment of loan amount and consequently artha tin suit was filed against him and the bank obtained a decree from the competent Adalat. The decree was put to execution and accordingly the Adalat allowed the application for publishing auction notice to sell the mortgaged property. In that moment, the petitioner had filed the application which was not maintainable under the aforesaid provisions of law and ratio laid by our Superior Court. Under the aforesaid premises, the Rule having no merit would be discharged. 

 6. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for opposite party 2, gone through the revisional application, grounds taken therein and ratio of the cases cited. It is admitted fact that the petitioner mortgaged the schedule land to the bank and took loan. It is also admitted that he defaulted in payment of the loan. It is also admitted that the suit has been filed against him and the bank obtained the decree. It is further admitted that the decree was put to execution in the aforesaid execution case. The question is whether the petitioner is entitled to get an order of the Adalat to sell the land in his private capacity. The provisions of rule 83(1) (2) and (3) of Order XXI of the Code is quoted below: 

 "(1) Where an order for the sale of immovable property has been made, if the judgment-debtor can satisfy the Court that there is reason to believe that the amount of the decree may be raised by the mortgage or lease or private sale of such property, or sonic part thereof, or of any other immovable property of the judgment-debtor, the Court may, on his application, postpone the sale of the property comprised in the order for sale on such terms and for such period as it thinks proper, to enable him to raise the amount. 

 Provided that all monies payable under such mortgage, lease or sale shall be paid, not to the judgment-debtor, but, save in so far as a decree-holder is entitled to set-off such money under the provisions of rule 72, into Court: 

 (3) Nothing in this rule shall be deemed to apply to a sale of property to be sold in execution of a decree for sale in enforcement of a mortgage of, or charge on, such property." 

 7. The provisions sub-rule 1 and 2 of rule 83 of the Order 21 is subject to the provisions of sub-rule 3. It is clear from the law that in execution of a decree for sale in enforcement of a mortgage or of charge on such property the provisions of rule 83(1) (2) of Order 21 shall not apply.
